data.why: The app ships its own built-in example set (eight curated polyphenols with backup SMILES in views/hierro.py, and a 'cabezas de serie' CID list) that works fully offline via text/SMILES entry, so no uploaded files are needed; the only file-upload paths in the app (Cribado general / Coordinacion) are gated behind a PubChem name/CID lookup that the sandboxed server cannot reach.

goals: Determine how a specific metal ion (Fe(III), Fe(II), Cu(II), Cu(I)) coordinates a given polyphenol, identify the bidentate O,O chelating sites, and see how mono/bis/tris speciation shifts with pH
Build a 3D mononuclear or polynuclear metal-polyphenol complex seed geometry from a chelation analysis, ready to hand off to DFT
Identify and number the coordinating heteroatoms (N, O, S, P) of a candidate ligand entered as SMILES, colored by donor strength, to plan a coordination study
Generate a force-field pre-optimized 3D geometry for a ligand and export ready-to-use Gaussian, ORCA, and Psi4 input files
Inspect ADMET/drug-likeness descriptors (Lipinski, Veber, Egan, logBB, QED, PAINS alerts) for a molecule as a priority filter before deeper analysis

review.summary: The part that was explored (metal–polyphenol chelation and speciation, complex-seed building, donor-atom numbering and 3D/QM input export) is accurate, sensibly structured, well labelled and backed by matching screens and an independent replay. But the tree leaves out the tool's headline purpose, retrieving and screening derivatives from databases, along with the coordination pipeline and the ADMET panel; it says so honestly, so the goal needs reframing and those stages need placeholders before filing.
